tonight.headline: Your 77% is still a read on their empty lineup, not on your roster.
body: Nothing has kicked off on either side. KEI returns still have five starters set and four slots empty — both wide receiver spots, the kicker and the defence — with Drake London, George Pickens, Parker Washington, Jalen Coker, the 49ers defence and Evan McPherson all sitting on their bench. Their projected 70.8 against your 121.1 is mostly those four zeroes, and that has now been true for four days.

Do not plan around it. If they set that lineup before Sunday morning they add roughly fifty points and this is a coin flip. Plan as though they will. The only decision on your side today is the quarterback slot, and the card below is the one that changed overnight.

case.label: What the four zeroes are worth
case.body: London 12.9, Pickens 14.8, McPherson 7.9 and the 49ers defence 7.4 is 43.0 projected points sitting on their bench, and their best remaining receiver options push it past fifty. Their 70.8 is not a bad roster, it is an unset one.

case.label: Your own margin
case.body: Your nine starters project 121.1 with Lawrence at quarterback. That is a middling week rather than a good one — you are 0-1 with 95.8 points for, ninth of ten in the league. The 77% is borrowed.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: KEI returns logging in before 11:00 Sunday Mexico City. There is no notification for this and nothing in the snapshot predicts it; the only thing you control is that your own nine are correct before Lawrence locks at 14:05.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — Lawrence locks 14:05 Sunday Mexico City
doFirst.title: Stafford in for Lawrence — this brief told you to do it last night and I am reversing that
doFirst.subtitle: The add was right. The start is not. Keep Trevor Lawrence in the quarterback slot.

case.label: What last night's card said
case.body: It read: 'IF STAFFORD LANDS: move Lawrence to the bench and Stafford into the QB slot before 14:05 Sunday, or Lawrence locks in at 14.9 and Stafford's 17.4 sits behind him on Monday.' You executed the add at 01:12 this morning, dropping Tyler Allgeier rather than MarShawn Lloyd. The add was correct. The instruction that came with it was built on the ESPN projection and nothing else.

case.label: What the reporting says instead
case.body: Yahoo's Week 2 quarterback board has Lawrence QB8 and Stafford QB14. Sports Illustrated's must-start list carries both but projects them QB14 and QB15, and gives Lawrence the evidence: 11 of 13 for four touchdowns and no interceptions on throws of ten or more yards downfield in Week 1, 78.3% completions, QB5 through one week. Stafford threw for 155 yards with no touchdown and an interception. Two independent weekly boards put Lawrence at or above Stafford; ESPN's projection is the only thing on the other side.

case.label: Stafford's case, stated honestly
case.body: It is real and it is environmental. Los Angeles are implied 27.5 at home against a Giants secondary missing Paulson Adebo to injured reserve with Deonte Banks (calf) and Greg Newsome II (rib) limited, and SI rate that defence 27th in EPA per pass allowed. Sharp put Stafford's Week 1 down to the Australia trip rather than decline. Jacksonville are implied 21.5 at a Denver defence Sharp grade better against the pass than the run. If you want the Monday-night leverage of knowing the score before your quarterback plays, this is the card that buys it — at the price of six ranking places.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Los Angeles put Stafford on a Saturday or Sunday report, which closes this entirely. Or Jacksonville downgrade Lawrence, which makes this a real card rather than a ghost. Either way the decision expires at 14:05 Sunday Mexico City, when Lawrence locks.

whatWentWrong.title: This brief told you to start Stafford over Lawrence on a projection
whatWentWrong.lead: The add was right and you made it at 01:12. The lineup instruction attached to it was never researched.

case.label: What happened
case.body: Last night's card was a ghost add — correctly, since claiming Stafford before 01:00 would have spent waiver priority that never resets in this league. It then attached a lineup instruction for Sunday that rested entirely on 17.4 against 14.9. No Week 2 quarterback board was consulted for either player.

case.label: What the board says
case.body: Yahoo: Lawrence QB8, Stafford QB14. SI: Lawrence QB14, Stafford QB15, both must-starts. The projection and the rankings point opposite ways and the projection was the only one in the brief.

case.label: Why this is the recurring shape
case.body: It is the same failure as the Rashee Rice tiles: a player graded and started for multiple runs without the number that decides him being reported. The fix is the same — the projection narrows the list, reporting decides.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If Stafford outscores Lawrence on Monday night, this reversal was wrong and the ESPN projection was the better instrument for two quarterbacks a fortnight into the season. That is the honest test and it settles on Monday.

whatWentWrong.title: One bench seat, four occupants, three days
whatWentWrong.lead: Stafford, then Charbonnet, then Allgeier, then Stafford again. That churn is why the card above is the only card today.

case.label: The sequence
case.body: 17 Sep 07:12 dropped Stafford for Charbonnet. 18 Sep 16:29 dropped Charbonnet for Allgeier. 19 Sep 07:12 dropped Allgeier for Stafford. The seat ended where it started, one player later, and STRATEGY section 3 names exactly this as value-destroying.

case.label: What it costs today
case.body: Your bench is Tuten, Lloyd, Mayer, Vele and Stafford, and four of the five arrived in the last three days. Every seat is inside the seven-day churn window, which is why Rico Dowdle and T.J. Hockenson are watch rows rather than cards. The roster has no clean place to put a good player.

case.label: The part that was not churn
case.body: The Stafford add itself cost only Tyler Allgeier, a body added the day before, and it spent no waiver priority. The mistake is the rotation, not this particular transaction.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing until 22 September, when the seven-day window on the earliest of these seats expires. If the Lamar trade lands before then, Tuten's seat opens without a drop and Hockenson becomes a straightforward add.

starting.name: Trevor Lawrence
starting.detail: JAX · at DEN · SUN 14:05 · he stays, reversing last night's instruction. Week 1 was 18 of 23 for 245 and four touchdowns, 11 of 13 on throws of ten-plus yards downfield with a 158.3 rating, and he is a QB1 scorer in nine straight games. Yahoo have him QB8 this week against Stafford's QB14. Jacksonville implied 21.5 as 2.5-point favourites; Sharp grade Denver better against the pass than the run, which is the argument against him and the reason the tile is not green.

starting.name: Jonathan Taylor
starting.detail: IND · at KC · SUN 18:20 · Daniel Jones · as much volume as exists: 88.7% snap share and 95.7% of backfield touches for 121 yards and two scores in Week 1. The matchup is the problem. Kansas City posted the highest run-defence success rate of Week 1 at 80%, on only 11 attempts faced, and Indianapolis are implied 20.0 against 26.5 — the underdog script that turns his carries into Daniel Jones dropbacks.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +1.0 on their best lineup and +2.5 on the one they actually have set — Tuten replaces Rachaad White, who they are starting at 7.6. Say that number in the message; it is what gets it read.

case.label: The surplus you are buying
case.body: Team 13 carry Lamar Jackson at slot 20 behind Josh Allen at slot 0. Verified against this morning's snapshot rather than assumed. In a one-quarterback league that is a top-3 quarterback producing nothing for them every single week, which is the structural surplus STRATEGY section 7 says to trade into.

case.label: Their hole, in their own slot column
case.body: Their running backs are Christian McCaffrey at 21.6 and then Rachaad White at 7.6 and Blake Corum at 9.1. Tuten at 10.1 is their best second back on the day he arrives. Check the slot column before believing this: White is at slot 2, a starter, and Corum is on their bench — so this genuinely improves the lineup they are running out.

case.label: What it does for you
case.body: Lamar 20.8 replaces Lawrence 14.9 at quarterback, and Tuten leaves a bench that has five men for five seats. On optimal lineups that is +3.4 for you against +1.0 for them. Tuten is the right piece to give because STRATEGY section 2 says flex-level players are close to worthless as assets in a 10-team league and difference-makers are not.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: The arithmetic is a one-week horizon and seasonProj has returned identical figures for five consecutive snapshots, so the season-long version of this cannot be priced at all. And the read on this manager has been wrong three runs running — the offer has now been sent nine times without a reply. LONGSHOT is the ceiling, not a hedge.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second real running back, which kills their gain. Or they trade or drop a quarterback, which kills the surplus. Or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report — he is not on this week's, checked against this morning's snapshot.

trades.copyText: Hi — you're carrying Lamar Jackson on your bench behind Josh Allen in a one-QB league, so he scores you nothing every week. I'd send Bhayshul Tuten (RB JAX, 10.1 this week, at Denver who were graded far worse against the run than the pass in Week 1) for him straight up. You're starting Rachaad White at 7.6 right now, so Tuten is a +2.5 upgrade to the lineup you actually have set, and you still keep McCaffrey and Corum. Happy to look at a different back if Tuten isn't the shape you want.

worthALook.name: T.J. Hockenson
worthALook.lead: Still the best free agent in a league whose flex takes a tight end, and still blocked by a bench with no clean seat.

case.label: Why he is the right shape
case.body: IPADE's flex is RB/WR/TE, so a second startable tight end has real value here and none in Chem. Hockenson is 65.0% rostered nationally, free here, and his ownership is rising 0.36 a day — the only one of these watch names moving up.

case.label: The new reason to want him
case.body: Kyler Murray was ruled out Friday with a concussion and Carson Wentz starts. Pro Football Rumors report Wentz had 'a much better connection with Jefferson and Hockenson' in his Week 1 snaps, and Wentz took 23 of Minnesota's 30 dropbacks. The quarterback change points his way, not away.

case.label: The constraint is the seat, not the player
case.body: Four of your five bench places changed hands in the last three days and every one is inside the seven-day churn window. Adding him today means dropping Mayer while Bowers is doubtful, or Tuten while he is the trade piece. Neither is right.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Colston Loveland drawing fewer than four targets against Minnesota today — that fires Loveland's own falsification clause and the tight end seat changes hands on Tuesday 22 September rather than the bench. Or the Lamar trade landing, which frees Tuten's seat without a drop.

worthALook.name: Jake Ferguson
worthALook.lead: 81.5% rostered nationally, a free agent here, and in the highest-total game on the board today.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: He cleared IPADE waivers unclaimed and has stayed free since. 81.5% rostered elsewhere and free here is the strongest wire band STRATEGY section 4 names, and this is the largest ownership gap on the wire.

case.label: The argument for him today
case.body: Dallas carry a 27.0 implied total in the 50.5-point Washington game, the highest on the Week 2 board. That is a tight end in the best scoring environment available, for nothing.

case.label: Why he is still a row and not a card
case.body: Same reason as Hockenson — there is no clean seat, and of the two Hockenson has the better role reporting this week. Taking a second free tight end while carrying Loveland and Mayer would be collecting the position rather than solving it.

case.label: When to act
case.body: CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens appearing on a Dallas injury report makes him the best free agent in this league and the seat is his that hour. Otherwise he waits behind Hockenson.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: Highest receiver season projection on the wire, free, and the wrong third Jaguar for this roster.

case.label: Availability, settled
case.body: Jacksonville's final Week 2 report has him limited with a thumb and playing, exactly as in Week 1. That question is closed and it was the open one.

case.label: The concentration problem
case.body: You already hold Trevor Lawrence and Bhayshul Tuten. STRATEGY section 8 names a Week 7 Jacksonville problem in this league by name — Tuten, the Jaguars defence and Cam Little all out together. A third Jaguar makes a scheduled hole worse for a marginal weekly gain.

case.label: Demoted from SOLID
case.body: He was a SOLID watch row last night. Nothing about him got worse; Hockenson's case got better with the Minnesota quarterback change, and only one of these can have the next seat.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If the Lamar trade lands, Tuten leaves, the Jacksonville concentration halves and Meyers becomes a straightforward add rather than a watch.

doNotChase.name: Rico Dowdle
doNotChase.lead: The biggest name to hit this wire all season, and the answer is still do not claim him. Waivers clear at 01:00 tonight Mexico City.

case.label: Why this is genuinely hard
case.body: Furia Regia dropped him at 05:39 this morning for Deebo Samuel. He is 85.7% rostered nationally with the highest season projection of any running back on this wire at 188.9, and the role reporting is the good kind: FantasyPros' Week 2 primer has him leading the Pittsburgh backfield at 57.8% of snaps and a 48.8% route share, with the only red-zone carry of Week 1. Snaps, routes and the goal line is the trio STRATEGY section 4 ranks first. This is the closest the waiver-priority question has come all season.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: He would not start for you. Jonathan Taylor at 18.5 and Saquon Barkley at 17.7 own the running back slots and Matthew Golden holds the flex at 10.9 against Dowdle's 10.1. Pittsburgh are implied 18.5, the second-lowest total on the Week 2 board. STRATEGY section 6 is explicit: spend priority in this league only on a player who starts immediately or is a genuine league-winner. He is neither, and he is splitting a backfield in one of the league's worst offences.

case.label: What the claim actually costs
case.body: Bloodsports sit 3rd of 10 and priority never resets here. A successful claim puts you last for the rest of the season, which is the chip you want available when a starting running back is lost in week 9 rather than when a committee back changes hands in week 2. You have spent none of it so far and that is the right record.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If nobody claims him by 01:00 tonight he becomes a FREE AGENT and costs nothing, which is exactly how Jake Ferguson reached this list — at that point take him over Devaughn Vele. Team 13 sit at priority 2 with only McCaffrey, Corum and White at running back, so expect them to have him first. And if Taylor or Barkley is ruled out before 01:00, the bar in section 6 is met and the claim goes in.

doNotChase.sources: FantasyPros · Steelers Depot · ESPN · Eat Drink and Sleep Football

doNotChase.name: Will Reichard
doNotChase.lead: The required weekly kicker comparison, answered: hold Jason Myers, and the honest version is that it costs you about a point.

case.label: The comparison, stated against you
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 board has Reichard K5 and Chase McLaughlin K6, both free agents here, against Jason Myers at K9. ESPN's projection disagrees and prefers Myers at 9.4. Two boards, two directions, and the incumbent loses the one that prices this week.

case.label: Why it holds anyway
case.body: The kicker seat changed hands at 07:06 on 18 September when Cam Little became Jason Myers — thirty hours ago. Moving it again today makes three kickers in four days. STRATEGY section 3 names rotating one seat through three players as the signature of optimising noise, and the gap is under a point in a position that swings five.

case.label: No new evidence either way
case.body: Still no Seattle scoring-environment reporting retrievable, a fourth consecutive run of trying. Seattle's 23.0 implied total is derived from the spread, not reported, and that is a weaker footing than this row would like.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers finishing outside the top twenty in Week 2 while Reichard or McLaughlin finish top five. The seat reopens on 22 September when the churn window expires, and the answer is whoever tops that week's board — as a free agent, never a claim.

doNotChase.sources: Pro Football Network · Eat Drink and Sleep Football · ESPN

doNotChase.name: Rams D/ST
doNotChase.lead: The required weekly defence comparison, answered: hold Baltimore. The 88.4%-owned name on this wire is not the upgrade it looks like.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Sports Illustrated's Week 2 start list has the Ravens against New Orleans. The Rams are the highest-owned free defence here at 88.4% and do not appear on that list at all; the Chargers do, and Green Bay and Chicago are named streaming options at 19.7% and 12.5%. None clears the incumbent.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: New Orleans are implied 19.0. The Rams host the Giants at 20.0 — a worse draw — and the same reporting has Los Angeles allowing the sixth-highest passing success rate of Week 1 with Myles Garrett on injured reserve. The ownership number is the only thing recommending them.

case.label: The standing rule
case.body: Never spend waiver priority on a defence in this league, regardless of what any board says. This one is free, so the rule is not even in play — the answer is still hold.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore finishing outside the top 12 defensive scores in Week 2. The seat then reopens on Tuesday and the answer is whoever tops that week's board, as a free agent.

doNotChase.sources: Sports Illustrated · Yahoo Sports · Eat Drink and Sleep Football

doNotChase.name: Zach Charbonnet
doNotChase.lead: You dropped him on Thursday, he is on waivers again tonight, and claiming him back would be the purest form of churn available.

case.label: Recorded so a familiar name is not read as an opportunity
case.body: He left this roster at 16:29 on 18 September. He is on WAIVERS clearing at 01:00 tonight, still OUT with the shoulder, still projecting 0.0.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: A claim would take Bloodsports from 3rd of 10 to last for the season on a 0.0 projection. No dated Seattle return has been published across six runs of looking.

case.label: Waiting dominates
case.body: If Seattle publish a return and he is activated, he is a free agent again and can be re-added for nothing. There is no branch where claiming beats waiting.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing that does not also make him free. The only cost of waiting is another manager taking him, and at 0.0 this week that cost is close to zero.

cannotSee.label: Whether Rico Dowdle gets claimed before you at 01:00 tonight
cannotSee.body: ESPN only ever returns your own pending claims. Team 13 sit at priority 2 with three running backs and are the obvious claimant, but that is a read on their roster rather than information. If he clears, he is free and the answer changes completely.

cannotSee.label: Whether KEI returns will set their lineup, which is the entire 77%
cannotSee.body: Four empty starting slots worth more than fifty projected points have been empty for four days. Nothing in the snapshot predicts whether that is inattention or a manager who logs in on Sunday morning.

cannotSee.label: Whether a failed waiver claim costs priority here
cannotSee.body: I believe an unsuccessful claim leaves priority intact in ESPN, which would make a losing Dowdle bid free. I could not verify that against this league's settings and the Dowdle decision above is written as though a claim costs priority whether or not it lands. If that belief is right, the case for bidding is stronger than this brief makes it.

cannotSee.label: Brock Bowers's actual Sunday status
cannotSee.body: DOUBTFUL with a pre-game workout to decide it. Michael Mayer's value this week turns on a decision Las Vegas make about ninety minutes before kickoff, and no snapshot taken today can contain it.

cannotSee.label: One tile is dashed
cannotSee.body: MarShawn Lloyd has no Jets-run-defence research this run. He projects 0.3 above your flex starter and that dash is exactly why the slot does not move on it.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are frozen, which undercuts the trade arithmetic
cannotSee.body: seasonProj has returned identical figures across five consecutive snapshots. The Lamar offer is therefore priced on one week, which is stated in its own risk block rather than hidden in this list.

cannotSee.label: No Seattle scoring-environment reporting, fourth run running
cannotSee.body: Jason Myers's 23.0 implied total is derived from the spread. Every other kicker input in this brief is a published ranking; his is an inference.

cannotSee.label: The two leagues do not score the same thing
